cands.name: Colby Watson

top: STAY AT HOME PARENT · Monroe, NC
money.note: Individuals gave $27,380; PAC money $1,750; candidate's own money $25,460. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Colby Watson is a Democratic candidate for U.S. House in North Carolina's 8th District. He is a homeschool graduate and a small business owner of more than a decade, with earlier work in masonry, construction and farming. He has not held public office.

endorsements.text: Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party (also listed in several Sway voting-group guides)

cands.gaps: We found no record of Colby Watson holding public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated position from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, abortion, or H-1B visas. His immigration statements are mixed: he supports border security and employer accountability alongside legal-immigration modernization, so we did not score them. We could not find what kind of business he owns or any detail on his work history beyond a general description. We found no controversies and no foreign ties. We found no employer or career records beyond his own descriptions.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Says he will work to stop Wall Street firms and large institutional investors from buying up neighborhoods; his campaign site lists this under Housing.

clean-money.evidence: Campaign site commitment: he will not accept money from lobbyists who represent corporate or foreign interests.

back-police-order.evidence: Says police are 'neighbors who run toward danger' and pledges to fund, train and stand with them; also pledges to hold violent offenders accountable.

second-amendment.evidence: Says he supports and will defend the Second Amendment and the right of law-abiding Americans to keep and bear arms; no specific policy on red flag laws, suppressors or purchase ages found.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Supports parents' right to choose their children's educational path (he was homeschooled and homeschools his own children) and says teachers should be paid what the job is worth; he also says he supports funding public schools and gives no position on vouchers or charters.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he wants to cut unnecessary red tape that blocks new homes and work with the market to increase starter-home supply; he gives no position on land conservation or growth limits.

cands.bio: Baptist pastor from Winston-Salem. Served as senior pastor of First Baptist Church in Charlotte and as president of the Baptist State Convention of North Carolina (2011–2013). Ran for Congress in 2014, 2016 and 2018. U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 8th District since January 2025.

controversies.text: Federal records show $20,000 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $19,574 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate.
Missed 0 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (0.0%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16.

In 2018 Harris's campaign employed operative McCrae Dowless. A February 2019 state hearing heard testimony of an unlawful absentee-ballot scheme, and the board unanimously ordered a new election. Harris said part of his testimony was wrong, citing a health issue. He didn't run again. WSOC reported a prosecutor found no evidence to charge him.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump endorsed Harris in the 2026 race and, as former president, in 2024.
Lt. Gov. Mark Robinson endorsed Harris in 2024.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Harris on data centers, development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, or limits on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land. We found no record of what he has said or done on suppressors, red-flag laws, H-1B visas, or teacher pay. We found no bills he has sponsored and no record of a foreign-government connection. His record on abortion restrictions in office is limited to his stated position. The Wikipedia page gives no source for some of its older quotes and sermons, so we did not use them.

votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.

votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he believes in the sanctity of all human life from conception to natural end.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says parents should decide how to educate their children, whether public, private, charter or homeschool, and that he supports a strong public education system. It does not mention a teacher pay raise.

second-amendment.evidence: In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey he said he will defend the Second Amendment. His 2018 campaign site opposed additional gun-ownership limits, saying strict gun laws do not reduce illegal use of firearms.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Yea on the Laken Riley Act, which requires DHS to detain certain people in the U.S. without legal permission who are arrested for burglary, theft, larceny or shoplifting; it passed the House 263-156 and was signed in January 2025.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he champions rigorous law enforcement and holding criminals accountable.
